summary: Training-free framework for vision-language models working in a Docker sandbox. Generated images (crops, masks, overlays) are registered in an addressable 'image ledger'. Only a bounded set of two active visual slots is sent to the model, and the model explicitly promotes the evidence it wants to see. Evaluated on seven visual QA/math benchmarks with four VLMs against a vanilla VLM and an append-every-image sandbox.

claims.claim: VLM-in-Sandbox achieves the highest sample-weighted accuracy for all four base VLMs.
claims.evidence: §4.1/Table 1: +1.66, +3.54, +5.09, +9.61pp over Vanilla VLM (GPT-4.1-mini, Gemini-2.5-Flash, Qwen3.5-9B, Ministral-3-8B); beats Sandbox Only in all 28 model-benchmark pairs. Single run per cell at temperature 1.0 in the broad study.

claims.claim: A compiler-matched 2x2 study reaches 66.27% accuracy with 18.6% fewer tokens than the retain-all control.
claims.evidence: §4.2/Fig. 4: +1.83pp vs Matched-Auto-All, 52 rescues / 29 regressions, bootstrap CI [0.40, 3.25], McNemar p=0.014; GPT-4.1-mini only, N=1,260. Model-directed selection over recency is not significant (p=0.185); bounded retention is the main token lever.

claims.claim: 302 rescues and 142 regressions versus Original Append-only across 6,350 GPT-4.1-mini examples.
claims.evidence: §4.3/Fig. 5: +2.52pp, 95% CI [1.83, 3.21]; three-run repeats only on two benchmarks.

claims.claim: The smaller workload reduces uncached tokens, TTFT and end-to-end latency under prefix caching.
claims.evidence: §5.2/Fig. 8: -16.4% uncached prompt tokens, -19.7% TTFT, -13.0% E2E vs Matched-Auto-All; one local vLLM backend, Qwen3.5-9B.

patterns.note: Bounded active context with addressable off-context artifact store reduces tokens 18.6% and slightly improves accuracy; recent-3-turns + deterministic recap cut tokens 8.6% (§5.1). Visual, not code, context.
Docker sandbox as execution backend; container lifecycle 0.82 s/example, 2% of E2E.
Model writes executable programs/tools in sandbox to generate evidence.

methodology.sample: 7 benchmarks, 6,350 examples (HRBench-4K, V*Bench, WeMath, MathVision-mini, MMStar, RealWorldQA, MMMU); matched study N=1,260.
methodology.baselines: Vanilla VLM and Original Append-only Sandbox; compiler-matched factorial controls. Related approaches compared only qualitatively (Appendix C).
methodology.variance: Paired bootstrap CIs and McNemar for GPT-4.1-mini; three runs per setting only on V*Bench and RealWorldQA.
methodology.ablations: 2x2 visibility-by-retention, slot capacity, history policy, step budget.
methodology.languages: n/a (visual QA; Python tools in sandbox).

verdict_reason: off-topic: a visual-reasoning sandbox for VLMs on image QA and math benchmarks, with no software-engineering or code-agent tasks. The evaluation is reasonable, with matched controls and paired tests, but the gains are modest (1.8–2.5pp in controlled comparisons) and no code is released.
applicability: Little transfers to a Java backend team ingesting and delivering the domain. The only portable idea is generic context hygiene: keep large intermediate artifacts in an addressable store outside the context, and expose a small bounded working set the agent explicitly promotes. That could inform how a harness handles large incoming documents or media assets, but this paper gives no evidence for that use, for multi-repo work or for spec-driven development.
